channel.title: The Dig — Software stack: compilers and pulse level
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Software stack: compilers and pulse level preset. Today's ranked reading list covers a scalable silicon spin-qubit architecture with logical operations (2611.33590), a 2D FPGA Union-Find decoder without global coordination (2611.33665), reproducible energy-relaxation distributions from broadband SWAP spectroscopy (2611.33854), high-throughput GPU decoding of quantum bivariate bicycle codes (2611.34481), and experimental quantum hardware benchmarks of flat non-Clifford hypergraph states on IBM Heron r2 (2611.34683), with the first three skimmed for transferable ideas and the latter two most directly informing HPC-assisted QEC and calibration-aware benchmarking for a small spin-qubit machine. No pay dirt today — 1 to skim.

item.title: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2
item.description:
Skim new result — Realized non-Clifford hypergraph states and contextuality games on Heron r2 QPUs, attaining a 3-qubit CCZ rotated Mermin-3 win rate of 83.95±0.29% (classical bound 75.00%) and beating the classical GHZ bound up to n=30 qubits (59.46±0.54% vs. 50.00%). Calibration-aware layout reaches a 96.85±0.09% raw win rate on the Mermin–Peres magic square.

Grade 0.412 · 2.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Noise-Adaptive Compiler Mappings for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Computers”

Figure

Win rates and margins across benchmarks on ibm_fez. Panels show Mermin-Peres magic square progression compared to Willow, GHZ parity game win rates versus classical ceilings up to 50 qubits, and non-Clifford CCZ and degree-3/4 parity witness advantages.

Asks

Can quantum nonlocal games and contextuality benchmarks be pushed past the Clifford-stabilizer regime to non-Clifford hypergraph states on superconducting processors?

Before

For Mermin-Peres magic square on superconducting processors, Google Willow achieved 98.30% raw win rate (Science 2026). Prior Clifford contextuality benchmarks were restricted to quadratic phase polynomials (deg⁡f≤2).

But

Single-chip benchmarks do not close relativistic locality loopholes. Finite-sample limits saturate direct X-basis total variation distance at 4,096 shots for n=16, and a coherence cliff occurs at Heavy-Hex depth 513 (0.00% return probability).

Tools

IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston) · Qiskit Runtime SamplerV2 · Lean 4-verified modular Walsh certifier · Barrier-protected Loschmidt echoes (U_f^† U_f)

Abstract

Real-hardware demonstrations of quantum contextuality have reached high precision on superconducting processors, exemplified by Google Quantum AI's Mermin-Peres magic square and stabilizer games on Willow (Science, 2026). Extending such benchmarks beyond the Clifford regime requires non-Clifford hypergraph states |ψ_f> = 2^-n/2 ∑_x (-1)^f(x) |x> governed by discrete algebraic invariants. Building on our Lean 4-verified framework of Modular Walsh Rigidity and Antipodal Obstructions, we present an experimental study on two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston) across 3 to 50 qubits and 11 auditable jobs (2.13 RUs total). First, we verify antipodal obstructions and mod-17 Walsh rigidity for degree-3/4 states (n=6,8,10), observing 5.4x-11.6x X-basis flatness separation between bent states, obstructed controls, and a degree-4 mod-3 fooler (W = +-1 mod 3), plus n=7 nonlinearity extraction (54.83 vs. 56.00). Second, barrier-protected Loschmidt echoes confirm non-Clifford coherence up to genuinely entangled 16-qubit degree-4 states (1,488x above random on ibm_fez; 17,296x on ibm_kingston for 2x8q, a 2.87x cross-chip gain) and locate a Heavy-Hex depth-513 coherence cliff. Third, calibration-aware layout raises the raw Mermin-Peres win rate on ibm_fez to 96.85 +- 0.09% raw (+87.4 sigma above 88.89% classical; 1.45 pp below Willow's 98.30% raw), while a tensored SPAM diagnostic reaches 98.35%. Uniformly random even-weight GHZ parity games beat the classical bound up to n=30 (89.44% [+79.4 sigma] at 6q to 59.46 +- 0.54% [+17.4 sigma] at 30q). Finally, 3-qubit CCZ rotated Mermin-3 (83.95 +- 0.29%, +31.2 sigma) and Hardy/Guhne-Cabello (77.15 +- 0.33%, +6.5 sigma) games strictly violate the exhaustive 75.00% LHV ceiling, and degree-3/4 antipodal parity witnesses achieve up to +45.87 pp (n=12) and +35.79 pp joint advantage on connected 16-qubit degree-4 states.

arxave:action.title: Adapt calibration-aware layout and SPAM diagnostics to the spin-qubit stack

item.arxave:action: Use the paper's calibration-aware layout scoring and tensored single-qubit SPAM diagnostic as a template for noise-aware transpilation and readout-error isolation on the 16-qubit spin QPU; validate the resulting layout choices against randomized benchmarking and readout-fidelity measurements.

arxave:action.title: Port the archived OpenQASM benchmark circuits to the native spin-qubit gate set

item.arxave:action: Extract the public OpenQASM 3.0 non-Clifford and GHZ parity-game circuits, transpile them to native CZ/CX/iSWAP gates, and run them as a periodic benchmark suite to detect drift and degradation.
